quickstart.title: Quick Start
quickstart.summary: Set up Theatarr and launch your first cinema session in just a few minutes.
quickstart.content:
## What is Theatarr?

Theatarr is a **cinema session orchestrator**. It automates your entire movie night: dimming the lights, playing trailers, displaying film information on your wall-mounted screen, starting the movie, and much more. It's like having a **personal stage manager** for your home cinema.

## Getting Started in 4 Steps

### 1. Connect a Media Service

Go to **Services** from the sidebar menu. Click **Add a service** and select your media player:

- **Plex**: enter the server URL and your API token
- **Jellyfin**: enter the server URL and your API key

Click **Test connection** to verify everything is working.

### 2. Add a Lighting Service

Still in **Services**, add a lighting service:

- **Philips Hue**: enter the bridge IP address and API key
- **WLED**: enter the controller IP address

### 3. Create Your First Session

Go to **Sessions** and click **New session**. Give your screening a name (e.g., "Marvel Night"), choose a date and select a movie from your library.

In the **workflow editor**, add sequences:

1. **Welcome**: lights dimmed to 40%, ambient music, waiting screen
2. **Trailer**: lights at 20%, trailer playback
3. **Movie**: lights off, movie playback
4. **End**: lights gradually turned back on, rating screen

### 4. Start the Session

On the day, open the session **dashboard** and click **Start**. Theatarr runs each sequence automatically. At any time you can **pause**, **skip to the next sequence** or **stop** the session.

> **Tip**: share the session's QR code with your guests so they can check in from their phone.

concepts.title: Key Concepts
concepts.summary: Understand the core concepts: sessions, sequences, actions, services and templates.
concepts.content:
## The Building Blocks of Theatarr

### Session

A **session** represents a complete cinema screening. It has a name, a scheduled date, an associated movie (or a selection mode) and a workflow that describes how the evening unfolds.

### Sequence (Block)

A **sequence** is a block of actions that execute **in parallel**. For example, a "Welcome" sequence can simultaneously dim the lights, play music and display a waiting screen.

Sequences execute one after another, in the order defined by the workflow.

### Action

An **action** is a single command sent to a service. There are 5 types of actions:

- **Lighting**: control lights (scenes, colors, brightness)
- **Audio**: play music or sounds
- **Media**: play a movie, trailer or pre-roll
- **Display**: show content on the wall-mounted screen (wallmount)
- **Actuator**: control home automation (curtains, motorized screen, fog machine)

### Service

A **service** is an external system connected to Theatarr:

- **Media sources**: Plex, Jellyfin (movie library)
- **Lighting**: Philips Hue, WLED (light control)
- **Metadata**: TMDB, Fanart.tv (movie information and images)
- **Actuators**: any home automation system exposed via API

### Template

A **display template** defines the wallmount layout (wall-mounted screen). It can display movie information, a countdown, posters and more.

### Workflow

The **workflow** is the visual editor that lets you build the flow of a session. You connect sequences to each other and add actions via drag and drop.

## How It All Works Together

```
Session → Workflow → Sequence 1 → [Action A + Action B + Action C] (parallel)
                   → Sequence 2 → [Action D + Action E] (parallel)
                   → Sequence 3 → ...
```

Each sequence waits for the previous one to finish before starting. Actions within the same sequence all start at the same time.

interface.title: Navigating the Interface
interface.summary: Discover the sidebar menu, user portal, wallmount and display options.
interface.content:
## Administration Interface

The admin interface is accessible after logging in with an administrator account. The **left sidebar menu** provides access to all sections:

- **Dashboard**: overview of upcoming sessions and recent activity
- **Sessions**: create, edit and control cinema sessions
- **Votes**: manage interactive votes and quizzes
- **Users**: create and manage accounts
- **Media**: trailers, pre-rolls, sounds and display templates
- **Services**: configure external connections (Plex, Hue, etc.)
- **History**: view past session history
- **Logs**: system logs for diagnostics
- **Settings**: general settings, export/import

## Top Bar

In the top right corner, you will find:

- **Language selector**: French, English, German, Spanish, Italian
- **Theme selector**: dark, light or automatic (follows system setting)
- **User menu**: profile and logout

## User Portal

Non-administrator users access the **portal**. It offers a simplified view with:

- Upcoming sessions they are invited to
- Ongoing votes
- Active quizzes
- Personal statistics (movies watched, votes participated in)

The portal is optimized for **smartphone** use.

## Wallmount (Wall-Mounted Screen)

The wallmount is a web page dedicated to display on a **TV or projector**. Access it via the `/wallmount` URL. This page displays:

- The waiting screen with the next movie
- Current movie information (poster, synopsis, rating)
- Countdown to the screening
- Vote or quiz results

The wallmount updates automatically via WebSocket, without needing to reload.

> **Tip**: open the wallmount in fullscreen mode (`F11` key) on your connected TV for an immersive experience.

session-create.title: Create a Session
session-create.summary: Step-by-step guide to create a cinema session with movie selection mode.
session-create.content:
## Create a New Session

From the **Sessions** menu, click **New session**.

### Basic Information

1. **Name**: give your screening a title (e.g., "Nolan Night", "Star Wars Marathon")
2. **Date and time**: schedule when the session starts
3. **Display template**: choose a template for the wallmount screen

### Movie Selection Mode

Theatarr offers three modes for choosing the movie:

#### Fixed Mode

The administrator directly selects the movie from the library. This is the simplest mode: you pick the film and everyone knows in advance what will be screened.

#### Vote Mode

Participants vote for the movie of their choice. Configure:

- The candidate movies (selected from your library)
- The maximum number of votes per person
- The vote opening and closing dates
- When the result is revealed

#### Mystery Mode

The movie remains secret until a chosen moment. Three sub-modes:

- **Random**: a random movie from your entire library
- **Filtered**: random but limited by genre, year or minimum rating
- **Curated**: chosen from a restricted list defined by the admin

### Add Participants

Select registered users who will participate in the screening. Each participant will receive an invitation and can:

- See the session in their portal
- Vote if vote mode is enabled
- Check in via the QR code on the day of the screening

### Finalize

After creation, you will be redirected to the **workflow editor** to build the flow of your session.

> **Tip**: you can duplicate an existing session to reuse a workflow that worked well.

session-workflow.title: Workflow Editor
session-workflow.summary: Build the flow of your session with the visual sequence and action editor.
session-workflow.content:
## The Visual Workflow Editor

The workflow editor is the central tool for building the scenario of your cinema session. It lets you visually organize sequences and actions.

### Workflow Structure

A workflow is composed of **sequences** (blocks) arranged vertically:

- Sequences execute **sequentially** (one after another)
- Actions within a sequence execute **in parallel** (all at the same time)

### Add a Sequence

Click **Add a sequence** at the bottom of the workflow. Give it a descriptive name (e.g., "Welcome", "Trailer", "Movie", "End").

### Add Actions

In each sequence, click **Add an action** and choose the type:

- **Lighting**: Hue scene, WLED effect, transition
- **Audio**: ambient music, alert sound
- **Media**: movie, trailer, pre-roll via Plex/Jellyfin
- **Display**: wallmount template, scrolling text
- **Actuator**: home automation command

### Rearrange with Drag and Drop

Use **drag and drop** to:

- Reorder sequences
- Move actions from one sequence to another
- Adjust the visual order of the workflow

### Transitions Between Sequences

Each sequence can define a transition type to the next one:

- **Fixed**: waits for a defined duration (e.g., 30 seconds)
- **Dynamic**: waits for the longest action to finish (e.g., end of trailer)
- **Manual**: waits for the operator to click "Next"

### Example Typical Workflow

| Sequence | Actions (in parallel) | Transition |
|----------|----------------------|------------|
| Welcome | Lights 40% + Music + Waiting screen | Manual |
| Trailer | Lights 20% + Trailer playback + Title display | Dynamic |
| Movie | Lights 0% + Movie playback | Dynamic |
| End | Lights 60% + Rating screen | Manual |

> **Tip**: start with a simple workflow (3-4 sequences) then enrich it over your movie nights.

session-vote-mode.title: Vote Mode
session-vote-mode.summary: Configure a session with movie selection by participant voting.
session-vote-mode.content:
## Configure Vote Mode

Vote mode lets your guests **choose the movie** for the evening. It's ideal for screenings among friends where everyone wants a say.

### Select Candidate Movies

From the vote configuration tab, browse your library and add the movies you want to put up for vote. You can add as many as you like, but **3 to 6 movies** is generally a good choice.

Each movie is displayed with its poster, rating and synopsis to help participants make their choice.

### Vote Settings

- **Votes per person**: how many movies each participant can select (1 to N)
- **Automatic opening**: the vote opens immediately or at a scheduled date
- **Scheduled closing**: date and time of automatic vote closure
- **Close when all have voted**: the vote closes as soon as all participants have voted
- **Show results during voting**: participants see scores in real time
- **Anonymous vote**: individual choices remain private

### Result Reveal

Two options for the reveal timing:

- **Immediate**: the result is visible as soon as the vote closes
- **Scheduled**: the result is revealed at a specific date/time (ideal for building suspense)

### Link a Vote to a Session

You can create an independent vote and then link it to a session, or create the vote directly from the session configuration. When a vote is linked, the winning movie is automatically assigned to the session.

### Share the Vote

Each vote generates **participation links** (tokens) that you can share with your guests, even those who don't have a Theatarr account. Participants access a dedicated page to vote from their phone.

> **Tip**: enable "close when all have voted" to avoid delaying the evening if everyone votes quickly.

session-mystery-mode.title: Mystery Mode
session-mystery-mode.summary: Keep the movie secret until the reveal with random, filtered or curated modes.
session-mystery-mode.content:
## Configure Mystery Mode

Mystery mode turns your movie night into a **surprise**. The film stays secret until a chosen moment, adding a dose of excitement to the screening.

### Three Sub-Modes Available

#### Random

A movie is selected **at random** from your entire library. This is the most adventurous mode: you might land on a forgotten classic or a hidden gem.

#### Filtered

The movie is chosen randomly but from a **filtered subset** of your library:

- **Genre**: action, comedy, sci-fi, horror, etc.
- **Period**: movies released between two years (e.g., 2000-2020)
- **Minimum rating**: only movies above a certain rating

This mode limits the surprises while keeping the mystery.

#### Curated

The administrator pre-selects a **restricted list** of movies (e.g., 5 films). The system will randomly choose one from this list. It's ideal when you want to control quality while maintaining the surprise effect.

### Reveal Date

Define the exact moment when the movie will be unveiled:

- **Before the screening**: reveal a few hours or days in advance (e.g., the day before at 8 PM)
- **At the start of the session**: the movie is revealed live on the wallmount when the session starts
- **During the session**: integrate the reveal into a workflow sequence for a dramatic effect

### Wallmount Display

Before the reveal, the wallmount displays a mystery screen with a question mark or a countdown. At the moment of the reveal, the movie poster appears with an animation.

### Combine with Other Features

Mystery mode can be combined with a **quiz** about the film after the screening, or with a **rating** to collect participant feedback.

> **Idea**: use filtered mode with the "Horror" genre for a surprise Halloween night!

session-control.title: Control a Session
session-control.summary: Control a session live: start, pause, navigate between sequences.
session-control.content:
## Control a Session Live

Once the session is scheduled and the workflow configured, you can control it in real time from the **control dashboard**.

### Access the Controls

From the **Sessions** page, open the desired session and click **Control** (or access directly if the session is in progress).

### Main Commands

- **Start**: launches the first sequence of the workflow
- **Pause**: suspends the current execution (timers stop)
- **Resume**: restarts after a pause
- **Next**: immediately skips to the next sequence (useful for manual transitions)
- **Stop**: ends the session and resets all services

### Real-Time Timeline

The dashboard displays a **timeline** showing:

- The currently executing sequence (highlighted)
- The progress of each action in the sequence
- Past and upcoming sequences
- Elapsed and estimated time

### QR Code and Check-In

Each session generates a unique **QR code**. Display it on the wallmount or print it to allow participants to:

- **Check in** by scanning the code from their phone
- Access session information
- Receive their virtual ticket

The control interface displays the list of checked-in participants in real time.

### Admin Scanner

The **admin scanner** lets you validate participant tickets at the entrance. Scan the ticket QR code to confirm attendance.

### Error Handling

If an action fails (e.g., disconnected service), the behavior depends on the configuration:

- **Continue**: the sequence continues despite the error
- **Stop**: the session stops, manual intervention required
- **Ignore**: the action is silently ignored

> **Tip**: keep one tab open with the session control and another with system logs to quickly diagnose issues.

action-overview.title: Actions Overview
action-overview.summary: The 5 action types, how sequences work and configuration options.
action-overview.content:
## The 5 Action Types

Each action in Theatarr corresponds to a command sent to a connected service. Here are the five available categories:

### 1. Lighting

Control your connected lights: Philips Hue scenes, WLED effects, gradual transitions. Ideal for setting the mood for your screening.

### 2. Audio

Play ambient music, sound effects or announcements. Control volume and crossfades.

### 3. Media

Play content via your connected media server: movies, trailers, pre-rolls. Theatarr controls Plex or Jellyfin to start playback.

### 4. Display

Show content on the wallmount: movie information, scrolling text, waiting screens, rating forms. Displays stack as layers.

### 5. Actuator

Send home automation commands: open/close curtains, lower the projection screen, activate the fog machine.

## How It Works in Sequences

In a sequence, all actions start **simultaneously**. This allows you to synchronize multiple effects:

- Dim the lights **at the same time** as launching the trailer
- Display the movie title **while** the music starts

## Common Options for All Actions

- **Delay**: wait time before the action executes (in seconds)
- **Error behavior**: what to do if the action fails
  - `Continue`: the sequence continues normally
  - `Stop`: the session stops for intervention
  - `Ignore`: the action is ignored without notification
- **Target service**: the external service that will execute the command

## Best Practices

- **Test your actions** individually before launching a full session
- Use the **Continue** behavior for non-critical actions (ambient lighting)
- Use **Stop** for essential actions (movie playback)
- Add a **delay** of 1-2 seconds between visual effects for a more natural result

> **Example**: a typical "Trailer" sequence contains 3 parallel actions: lights at 20%, trailer playback, and title display on the wallmount.

action-lighting.title: Lighting Actions
action-lighting.summary: Control Philips Hue and WLED lights to create the perfect ambiance.
action-lighting.content:
## Compatible Lighting Services

### Philips Hue

Connect your Philips Hue bridge to control your bulbs and LED strips. You can use:

- **Preset scenes**: select from scenes configured in the Hue app
- **Brightness**: adjust intensity from 0% (off) to 100%
- **Transition**: fade duration between current and new state

### WLED

Control your addressable LED strips via WLED:

- **Effects**: choose from dozens of built-in effects (rainbow, breathe, fire, etc.)
- **Colors**: set the primary color
- **Brightness**: adjust LED intensity

## Configuring a Lighting Action

1. Select the **target service** (your Hue bridge or WLED controller)
2. Choose the **command type**: scene, brightness, effect
3. Set the **parameters** according to the chosen type
4. Optional: add a **transition duration** for a gradual fade

## Practical Examples

Here is a typical scenario for a movie night:

| Sequence | Lighting | Detail |
|----------|----------|--------|
| Welcome | Warm ambiance | Hue scene "Relax", 40% |
| Trailer | Gradual dimming | Brightness 20%, blue, 3s transition |
| Movie | Complete darkness | Brightness 0%, 5s transition |
| Intermission | Soft ambiance | Hue scene "Evening", 35% |
| End | Lights back on | Brightness 60%, warm white, 8s transition |

## Tips

- Create **dedicated scenes** in the Hue app for your movie nights
- Use a **long transition** (5-10 seconds) for dimming before the movie: the effect is much more immersive than an abrupt switch-off
- Combine **Hue** (ceiling) and **WLED** (TV backlight) for layered lighting
- Always test your scenes from Theatarr before the screening to avoid surprises

> **WLED tip**: the "Breathe" effect in dark blue is ideal during trailers for a cinematic look.

action-audio.title: Audio Actions
action-audio.summary: Play ambient music, manage volume and crossfades.
action-audio.content:
## Audio Actions

Audio actions let you play music or sound effects during your cinema session.

### Audio Content Types

- **Ambient music**: set the atmosphere before the screening begins
- **Sound effects**: gong, bell, audible countdown
- **Announcements**: pre-recorded messages (e.g., "The screening is about to begin")

### Configuring an Audio Action

1. **Audio file**: select a file from your sound library (uploaded via the Media section)
2. **Volume**: set playback volume (0-100%)
3. **Fade in**: duration in seconds to gradually raise the volume
4. **Fade out**: duration in seconds to gradually lower the volume

### Managing Pre-rolls and Sounds

Before you can use audio actions, you need to upload your files in the **Media > Pre-rolls and Music** section. Common formats are supported (MP3, WAV, OGG, etc.).

Organize your files by category:

- `ambiance/`: waiting music
- `effects/`: short sounds and effects
- `announcements/`: voice messages

### Typical Use Cases

#### Before the Screening

Play an ambient playlist while guests settle in:

- Volume: 40%
- Fade in: 3 seconds
- In the "Welcome" sequence

#### Transition to the Movie

Fade out the music before the trailer starts:

- Fade out: 5 seconds
- Combines with light dimming

#### After the Screening

End-of-session music while the lights come back on:

- Volume: 30%
- Fade in: 2 seconds

### Best Practices

- Use a **moderate volume** (30-40%) for ambient music: it should accompany, not dominate
- Plan a **fade out** before each transition to avoid abrupt cutoffs
- Test the sound level under the actual conditions of your setup

> **Idea**: use the soundtrack of the movie being screened as ambient music to set the atmosphere.

action-media.title: Media Actions
action-media.summary: Play movies, trailers and pre-rolls via Plex or Jellyfin.
action-media.content:
## Media Actions

Media actions let you **play video content** on your connected media player (Plex or Jellyfin).

### Content Types

- **Movie**: the session's main movie, played from your library
- **Trailer**: movie trailer for the featured or another film
- **Pre-roll**: custom intro video (logo, warning, animation)

### Configuring a Media Action

1. **Service**: select your player (Plex or Jellyfin)
2. **Content type**: movie, trailer or pre-roll
3. **Content selection**:
   - Movie: automatically linked to the session's movie
   - Trailer: manual, automatic or rule-based selection
   - Pre-roll: select from the pre-roll library

### Trailer Selection

Three trailer selection modes:

- **Manual**: you choose exactly which trailer to play
- **Automatic**: Theatarr selects the trailer for the session's movie
- **Rule-based**: selection based on criteria (genre, year, popularity)

### Playback Control

During the session, Theatarr controls your media player:

- Automatic playback start
- Pause and resume synchronized with the session
- Clean stop at the end of the sequence

### Example Workflow with Media

| Sequence | Media action | Duration |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| Intro | Pre-roll "Welcome" | 15 sec |
| Trailer 1 | Movie trailer | ~2 min |
| Trailer 2 | Recommended trailer | ~2 min |
| Movie | Main movie playback | Dynamic |

### Best Practices

- Use the **Dynamic** transition for sequences containing media: the sequence will automatically advance when playback is finished
- Download trailers in advance via the **Media > Trailers** section to avoid loading times
- Test playback on your Plex/Jellyfin client before the screening to verify the content is accessible

> **Tip**: combine a custom pre-roll with a light fade for a real cinema-worthy intro.

action-display.title: Display Actions
action-display.summary: Manage wallmount display: templates, scrolling text, animations and layer system.
action-display.content:
## Display Actions

Display actions control what appears on the **wallmount** (wall-mounted screen) during the session.

### Display Templates

Each display action uses a **template** that defines the layout. Built-in templates include:

- **Waiting screen**: poster, movie title, countdown
- **Movie information**: synopsis, rating, genres, duration
- **Vote results**: movie ranking with scores
- **Rating screen**: post-screening feedback form

### Scrolling Text

Add scrolling text with various **animations**:

- `scroll`: classic horizontal scrolling
- `blink`: blinking
- `pulse`: gentle pulsation
- `fade`: gradual appear/disappear
- `neon`: luminous neon effect
- `shimmer`: sparkling

Customize with options:

- **Font**: font family selection
- **Weight**: normal, bold, extra-bold
- **Position**: top, center, bottom of screen
- **Color**: text and background color

### Layer System

The wallmount display uses a **layer system** with z-index. Multiple display actions can stack on top of each other:

- Layer 0: background (e.g., image or gradient)
- Layer 1: movie information (poster, title)
- Layer 2: scrolling text (announcements)

Each layer is independent and can be added or removed separately.

### Feedback Screen

After the screening, display a **feedback collection** screen where participants can rate the movie and leave a comment from their phone.

### Configuration

1. **Display type**: template, scrolling text, feedback screen
2. **Template**: template selection
3. **Layer (z-index)**: position in the display stack
4. **Duration**: display time (or permanent until the next sequence)

> **Tip**: use scrolling text with the `neon` animation to display "The screening is about to begin" just before the movie starts -- guaranteed effect!

action-actuator.title: Actuator Actions
action-actuator.summary: Control home automation: curtains, motorized screen, fog machine and other devices.
action-actuator.content:
## Actuator Actions

Actuator actions let you **control home automation devices** from your cinema sessions. Any device exposed via an API can be integrated.

### Compatible Devices

Here are examples of devices you can control:

- **Motorized curtains**: open/close room curtains
- **Projection screen**: lower/raise the motorized screen
- **Projector**: turn on/off, change source
- **Fog machine**: trigger a fog effect for ambiance
- **Ventilation**: activate/deactivate air conditioning or ventilation
- **Smart plugs**: turn devices on/off

### Configuring an Actuator Action

1. **Service**: select the connected home automation service
2. **Command**: name of the command to send (e.g., `close`, `open`, `on`, `off`)
3. **Value** (optional): additional parameter (e.g., 50% position for a curtain)

### Integration with Home Automation Systems

Theatarr can communicate with any system exposing an **HTTP API**. Common integrations include:

- **Home Assistant**: via the REST API
- **Domoticz**: via the JSON API
- **Any custom system**: as long as it exposes HTTP endpoints

The actuator service in Theatarr is generic: you define the base URL and the specific commands to send.

### Example Complete Scenario

| Sequence | Actuator | Command |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Welcome | Projection screen | Lower |
| Welcome | Curtains | Close |
| Movie | Projector | Source HDMI 2 |
| End | Curtains | Open (50%) |
| End | Projection screen | Raise |

### Best Practices

- Add a **delay** between mechanical actuator commands (curtains, screen) to avoid overloads
- Use the **Continue** error behavior for non-critical actuators
- Test each command individually from the **Services** page before integrating them into a workflow
- Plan a **reset sequence** at the end of your session (raise screen, open curtains)

> **Tip**: combine closing the curtains with dimming the lights in the same sequence for a synchronized "movie theater" effect.

vote-create.title: Create a Vote
vote-create.summary: Configure a vote with movies, participants, schedule and privacy options.
vote-create.content:
## Create a Vote

From the **Votes** menu, click **New vote** to create a voting session.

### Basic Information

1. **Name**: vote title (e.g., "Movie Choice - Saturday March 15")
2. **Description** (optional): context or instructions for voters

### Movie Selection

Browse your library and add the movies to propose. For each movie, participants will see:

- The movie poster
- Title and release year
- TMDB rating
- Synopsis in the configured language
- Genres

### Participants

Two types of participants:

- **Registered users**: select from existing Theatarr accounts
- **Guests (tokens)**: generate participation links for people without an account

Each token link is unique and single-use.

### Vote Settings

- **Maximum votes per person**: number of movies each participant can choose
- **Open immediately**: the vote is open as soon as it's created
- **Show results during voting**: participants see scores live
- **Anonymous vote**: individual choices are not visible
- **Restricted access**: only invited participants can vote
- **Scheduled closing**: automatic closing date and time
- **Close when all have voted**: automatic closure when the last participant has voted

### Reveal Schedule

Define when the result will be visible:

- **Upon closing**: immediate result
- **Scheduled date**: the result is revealed at a specific time

### After Creation

Once the vote is created, you can:

- **Copy links** to share with participants
- **Track votes** in real time from the dashboard
- **Open/close** the vote manually
- **Link the vote** to a cinema session

> **Tip**: create the vote a few days before the screening and share the links via message or email to give everyone time to vote.

vote-manage.title: Manage Votes
vote-manage.summary: Open, close, track live results and link a vote to a session.
vote-manage.content:
## Manage Ongoing Votes

From the **Votes** page, access each vote's dashboard to control it in real time.

### Open and Close the Vote

- **Open**: makes the vote accessible to participants. If the "Open immediately" option was not checked at creation, open it manually when you're ready.
- **Close**: closes the vote. No new votes will be accepted. Closing can also be automatic (scheduled date or when all have voted).

### Generate Share Links

For each vote, generate **participation tokens**:

1. Click **Generate links**
2. Choose the number of links to create
3. Copy and share the links via email, SMS or messaging

Each link opens a dedicated page where the participant can view movies and vote, even without a Theatarr account.

### Track Results in Real Time

The vote dashboard displays:

- The number of participants who have already voted
- Movie ranking by number of votes
- Results chart (if display is enabled)
- Participant list and their status (voted / pending)

If the **Show results during voting** option is enabled, participants also see this information.

### Result Reveal

The reveal can happen in two ways:

- **Automatic**: at the scheduled date or upon closing
- **Manual**: click **Reveal** to display the result

The reveal can be broadcast on the **wallmount** for a spectacular effect during the evening.

### Link a Vote to a Session

From the vote page or from a session's configuration, you can **link** a vote to a session. The winning movie will then be automatically assigned as the session's movie.

This linking allows integrating the vote result directly into the session workflow.

> **Tip**: schedule the vote reveal at the start of the session for a suspenseful moment in front of the wallmount.

quiz-create.title: Create a Quiz
quiz-create.summary: Add questions manually with multiple choice, hints and time limits.
quiz-create.content:
## Create a Quiz Manually

Quizzes are a fun way to liven up your movie nights. Create questionnaires about movies, actors, iconic quotes or any other topic.

### Create a New Quiz

From the **Votes** menu (which also manages quizzes), click **New quiz**.

### Basic Information

1. **Name**: quiz title (e.g., "Marvel Quiz", "Cinema Blind Test")
2. **Description**: instructions or quiz theme

### Add Questions

For each question, configure:

- **Question text**: the question asked to participants
- **Answer choices**: 2 to 6 answer options
- **Correct answer**: check the right answer
- **Hint** (optional): a hint displayed if the participant hesitates
- **Time limit**: maximum time to answer (e.g., 15, 30 or 60 seconds)

### Question Example

```
Question: In which movie can you hear "I am your father"?

Choices:
  A) Star Trek
  B) Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back ✓
  C) Back to the Future
  D) Indiana Jones

Hint: It's a film from the saga created by George Lucas.
Time: 20 seconds
```

### Quiz Options

- **Live results**: participants see the leaderboard after each question
- **Anonymous**: individual scores are not displayed publicly
- **Auto-advance**: moves to the next question automatically after time runs out
- **Feedback between questions**: shows the correct answer and statistics before continuing

### Flow

Once the quiz is created and opened:

1. Participants join via the portal or a link
2. Questions are displayed one at a time
3. Everyone answers within the time limit
4. Scores accumulate
5. The final leaderboard is displayed

### Integration with a Session

Integrate a quiz as a sequence in your session workflow. For example, launch a quiz between two trailers or after the screening.

> **Idea**: create a quiz about the movie that was just screened to test your guests' attention!

quiz-ai.title: AI Quiz Generator
quiz-ai.summary: Automatically generate questions via The Trivia API with category and difficulty selection.
quiz-ai.content:
## Generate a Quiz Automatically

Theatarr integrates **The Trivia API** to automatically generate quiz questions. It's a quick way to create a quiz without writing each question manually.

### How It Works

1. From quiz creation, click **Generate with AI**
2. Configure the generation parameters
3. Preview the questions
4. Customize if needed
5. Confirm to create the quiz

### Generation Parameters

#### Category

Choose from available categories:

- **Film & TV**: questions about cinema and TV shows (ideal for your movie nights)
- **Music**: artists, albums, songs
- **Science**: physics, chemistry, biology
- **History**: historical events, figures
- **Geography**: countries, capitals, culture
- **Sports**: competitions, athletes, records
- **Art & Literature**: works, authors, movements
- And many more...

#### Difficulty

- **Easy**: questions accessible to everyone
- **Medium**: questions requiring good general knowledge
- **Hard**: questions for experts
- **Mixed**: a mix of all difficulties

#### Number of Questions

Choose between 5 and 30 questions per quiz. For a movie night, **10 to 15 questions** is a good balance between entertainment and duration.

#### Tags (optional)

Refine the selection with specific keywords (e.g., "Marvel", "90s", "Oscar").

### Preview and Customization

Before confirming, you can:

- **Preview** each generated question
- **Remove** questions you don't like
- **Edit** the text or answers
- **Add** your own questions to the generated batch
- **Regenerate** to get new questions

### Important Note

The Trivia API is a free service and questions are **in English**. This may work for an English-speaking audience, or you can use the questions as a base and translate them manually.

> **Tip**: generate questions in the "Film & TV" category then customize them by adding specific questions about the evening's movie.

trailers.title: Trailer Management
trailers.summary: Browse, search and download trailers from YouTube.
trailers.content:
## Trailer Library

Theatarr manages a library of **trailers** that you can use in your cinema sessions. Access it from **Media > Trailers**.

### Browse the Library

The trailers page displays all available trailers with:

- Video thumbnail
- Associated movie title
- Trailer duration
- Quality (resolution)
- Download date

Use the **search bar** to quickly find a trailer by movie title.

### Download a Trailer

To add a trailer to your library:

1. Click **Download**
2. Search for the movie by title
3. Select the desired trailer from YouTube results
4. Choose the download quality
5. Start the download

The download happens in the background. You can continue using Theatarr in the meantime.

### Storage Statistics

The page displays **storage statistics**:

- Total number of trailers
- Disk space used
- Average file quality

### Automatic Download

You can configure **automatic download rules** (see the dedicated article) so that Theatarr automatically downloads trailers for movies in your library.

### Using in Sessions

Once a trailer is downloaded, it's available for media actions in your sessions. You can:

- Manually select a trailer in an action
- Let Theatarr automatically choose the session movie's trailer
- Play multiple trailers in sequence (just like at the cinema!)

> **Tip**: download trailers in advance to avoid wait times on the day of the screening and ensure smooth playback.

trailer-rules.title: Automatic Rules
trailer-rules.summary: Create rules to automatically download trailers based on specific criteria.
trailer-rules.content:
## Automatic Download Rules

Automatic rules allow Theatarr to **download trailers without manual intervention**, based on criteria you define.

### Create a Rule

From **Media > Trailers > Rules**, click **New rule**.

### Filter Criteria

Define which movies are eligible for automatic download:

- **Genre**: action, comedy, drama, sci-fi, horror, etc. (one or more)
- **Period**: minimum and/or maximum release year (e.g., only movies after 2010)
- **Popularity**: minimum popularity score (based on TMDB)
- **Language**: original language of the movie

### Rotation and Retention

Manage disk space with rotation options:

- **Keep the N most recent**: only keeps the most recently downloaded trailers
- **Keep the N most played**: keeps the trailers most used in your sessions
- **No limit**: keeps all trailers (watch your disk space)

### Quality

Define the minimum desired quality:

- 720p: standard quality, smaller file size
- 1080p: HD quality, good compromise
- 4K: best quality, large files

### Limits per Execution

Set the **maximum number of downloads** per rule execution to control bandwidth and disk space usage.

### Rule Examples

#### "New Action Movies" Rule

- Genre: Action, Sci-fi
- Period: 2020 and later
- Rotation: keep the 20 most recent
- Quality: 1080p minimum
- Max downloads: 5 per execution

#### "Classics" Rule

- Genre: all
- Period: 1970-2000
- Popularity: score > 50
- Rotation: keep the 10 most played
- Quality: 720p minimum

### How It Works

Rules are automatically executed by the Theatarr scheduler. Each execution checks for new movies in your library and downloads trailers matching the criteria.

> **Tip**: start with a simple rule and adjust the criteria over time based on your needs and available disk space.

prerolls-sounds.title: Pre-rolls and Music
prerolls-sounds.summary: Upload and organize your intro videos and ambient audio files.
prerolls-sounds.content:
## Pre-rolls and Music

Theatarr lets you upload and manage media files to enrich your cinema sessions.

### Video Pre-rolls

Pre-rolls are **short intro videos** played before the movie, just like in a real cinema. Examples:

- Your "home cinema" logo
- "Turn off your phones" animation
- Countdown before the movie
- Movie rating (age warning)

#### Upload a Pre-roll

1. Go to **Media > Pre-rolls and Music**
2. Click **Add a file**
3. Select your video file (MP4, MKV, AVI supported)
4. Give it a name and category

### Audio Files

Audio files serve as **ambient music** or **sound effects** during sessions:

- Waiting music before the screening
- Movie soundtrack as background
- Sound effects (start gong, applause)
- Pre-recorded voice announcements

#### Supported Formats

- Audio: MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC, AAC
- Video: MP4, MKV, AVI, WebM

### Organize by Category

Sort your files by category for easy retrieval:

- **Intros**: opening video pre-rolls
- **Ambiance**: waiting and background music
- **Effects**: short sounds and special effects
- **Announcements**: voice messages

### Use in Sessions

Once uploaded, your files are available in workflow actions:

- **Media action**: select a pre-roll for an intro sequence
- **Audio action**: choose an audio file for ambiance or effects

### Best Practices

- Keep pre-rolls **short** (10-30 seconds) to avoid boring the audience
- Prepare several ambient tracks to vary from one screening to another
- Name your files descriptively (e.g., "home-cinema-intro-v2.mp4")
- Test the audio levels of your files to ensure consistency

> **Idea**: create a custom pre-roll with your home cinema's name and a stylish animation -- free tools like Canva or DaVinci Resolve make it easy.

templates.title: Display Templates
templates.summary: Manage wallmount templates: layout, movie information and countdown.
templates.content:
## Display Templates

Display templates define the **wallmount layout** -- what your viewers see on the wall-mounted screen or projector.

### Built-in Templates

Theatarr offers **ready-to-use templates** that you can activate immediately. To load them, go to **Media > Templates** and click **Initialize built-in templates**.

Built-in templates cover the most common use cases:

- **Waiting screen**: displays the next movie with a countdown
- **Movie presentation**: poster, synopsis, rating, genres and duration
- **Vote results**: movie ranking with vote counts
- **Mystery**: screen with question mark and countdown

### Activate a Template

A template can be activated **globally** to serve as the default template. This template will be used by the wallmount when no session is in progress.

1. Open the desired template
2. Click **Activate**
3. The template becomes the wallmount's active template

### Displayed Information

Templates can display the following data:

- **Movie poster**: main poster and alternative posters (via Fanart.tv)
- **Title and year**: movie title and release year
- **Synopsis**: summary (via TMDB)
- **Rating**: movie score (TMDB)
- **Genres**: movie categories
- **Duration**: runtime in hours and minutes
- **Logos**: high-quality movie logo (via Fanart.tv)
- **Backdrops**: cinematic background images
- **Countdown**: time remaining before the screening starts

### Template Management

From the management page, you can:

- **View** available templates
- **Activate/deactivate** a template
- **Delete** a custom template

### Automatic Enrichment

The displayed information (posters, synopsis, logos) comes from the **automatic enrichment** of movies via TMDB and Fanart.tv. Make sure these services are configured for optimal display.

> **Tip**: activate a waiting screen template so your wallmount always looks great, even between screenings.

service-connect.title: Connect a Service
service-connect.summary: Add and configure an external service: type selection, URL, API key and connection test.
service-connect.content:
## Connect an External Service

Theatarr communicates with external services to control your equipment. Each service is connected via a specific **adapter**.

### Add a New Service

From **Services**, click **Add a service**.

### Step 1: Choose the Category

Select the service type:

- **Media source**: content server (Plex, Jellyfin)
- **Lighting**: light controller (Philips Hue, WLED)
- **Player**: playback device
- **Actuator**: home automation system
- **Metadata**: movie information provider (TMDB, Fanart.tv)

### Step 2: Select the Adapter

Choose the adapter corresponding to your equipment. The list of available adapters depends on the selected category.

### Step 3: Configure the Connection

Enter the connection details:

- **Name**: a descriptive name (e.g., "Plex Living Room", "Hue Cinema")
- **URL / IP Address**: the service address (e.g., `http://192.168.1.100:32400`)
- **API Key / Token**: the service's authentication token

Each adapter has its own configuration fields.

### Step 4: Test the Connection

Click **Test connection** to verify that Theatarr can communicate with the service. The test checks:

- Network accessibility
- Authentication
- Available features (capabilities)

### Enable / Disable

A service can be **temporarily disabled** without being deleted. This is useful for debugging or when equipment is under maintenance.

### Getting Your API Keys

| Service | Where to find the key |
|---------|----------------------|
| Plex | Settings > Account > Token (in the XML URL) |
| Jellyfin | Dashboard > API Keys > Create |
| Philips Hue | Press the bridge button then call the API |
| WLED | No key needed (access by IP) |
| TMDB | Create an account on themoviedb.org > API |
| Fanart.tv | Create an account on fanart.tv > API Key |

> **Tip**: always test the connection after configuration. If the test fails, check the IP address and make sure the service is on the same network.

service-types.title: Service Types
service-types.summary: Detailed overview of each type: media sources, lighting, metadata and actuators.
service-types.content:
## Supported Service Types

Theatarr supports several categories of external services, each with its specific adapters.

### Media Sources

Media sources provide your movie library and the ability to play content.

#### Plex

- **Library**: access to your movies, series and trailers
- **Playback**: launch content on your Plex clients
- **Metadata**: retrieve information about your media
- Configuration: server URL + Plex token

#### Jellyfin

- **Library**: browse your media
- **Playback**: control playback on Jellyfin clients
- **Open API**: no license restrictions
- Configuration: server URL + API key

### Lighting

#### Philips Hue

- **Scenes**: activate preset scenes
- **Individual control**: brightness, color, temperature per bulb or group
- **Transitions**: gradual fades between states
- Configuration: bridge IP + API key

#### WLED

- **LED effects**: dozens of addressable light effects
- **Colors**: full RGB color palette
- **Segments**: control portions of the LED strip
- Configuration: controller IP (no key needed)

### Metadata

#### TMDB (The Movie Database)

- **Information**: titles, synopses, release dates
- **Ratings**: average scores and popularity
- **Genres**: movie categorization
- **Images**: official posters and backdrops
- Configuration: TMDB API key (free)

#### Fanart.tv

- **HD logos**: high-resolution movie logos
- **Alternative posters**: community-created posters
- **Backdrops**: cinematic wallpapers
- **Extra artwork**: banners, thumbnails, clearart
- Configuration: Fanart.tv API key (free)

### Actuators

Actuators are **generic** adapters for home automation. They communicate via HTTP API calls and can control any connected device: curtains, motorized screens, projectors, etc.

> **Tip**: start by connecting a media service (Plex or Jellyfin) and TMDB -- that's the minimum to enjoy Theatarr.

service-libraries.title: Libraries and Enrichment
service-libraries.summary: Select movie libraries and enrich metadata with TMDB and Fanart.tv.
service-libraries.content:
## Libraries and Enrichment

Once your media services are connected, configure the libraries to use and enrich your movie information.

### Select Libraries

Your media server (Plex/Jellyfin) typically contains several libraries (Movies, Series, Documentaries...). In Theatarr, select the **movie** libraries you want to use.

From the media service page, you can:

1. View detected libraries
2. Enable/disable each library
3. Sync the movie list

### Movie Enrichment

Enrichment adds **additional metadata** to your movies. Two services are available:

#### TMDB (The Movie Database)

TMDB provides:

- **Translated synopsis**: full movie description
- **Genres**: categorization (Action, Comedy, Drama, etc.)
- **Rating**: average TMDB user score
- **Release date**: original and local release dates
- **Official posters**: high-resolution posters
- **Backdrops**: background images from movie scenes

#### Fanart.tv

Fanart.tv complements with premium visuals:

- **HD logos**: high-resolution movie logos (perfect for the wallmount)
- **Alternative posters**: community-created posters
- **Additional backdrops**: extra wallpapers
- **ClearArt**: artistic movie renderings

### Automatic Enrichment

When a new movie is detected in your library, Theatarr can **automatically** launch enrichment. The process:

1. Movie detected in library
2. TMDB search by title and year
3. Retrieval of metadata
4. Fanart.tv search for visuals
5. Storage of enriched data

### Manual Enrichment

You can also manually enrich a movie from its page:

1. Open the movie in the list
2. Click **Enrich**
3. Verify the TMDB match
4. Data is updated

### Enrichment Status

Each movie displays an enrichment indicator:

- **Complete**: TMDB + Fanart.tv available
- **Partial**: only TMDB or only Fanart.tv
- **Not enriched**: no external metadata

> **Tip**: configure TMDB and Fanart.tv from the start so all your movies are automatically enriched with quality visuals.

config-general.title: General Settings
config-general.summary: Configure language, theme, SMTP notifications and application options.
config-general.content:
## General Settings

Access settings from **Settings > Parameters** in the sidebar menu.

### Interface Language

Theatarr is available in **5 languages**:

- French (default)
- English
- German
- Spanish
- Italian

Language changes are instant and affect the entire interface. The language is saved per user.

> **Note**: the interface language is independent from the metadata language (always French by default for TMDB).

### Display Theme

Three theme options:

- **Dark**: black background, ideal for use in the dark
- **Light**: white background, better readability in bright light
- **System**: automatically follows your device's theme

The theme is configurable from the **selector** in the top right of the interface or from the settings.

### SMTP Configuration

Configure an SMTP server to send **email notifications**:

- **SMTP server**: server address (e.g., `smtp.gmail.com`)
- **Port**: server port (587 for TLS, 465 for SSL)
- **Username**: sending email address
- **Password**: password or app password
- **Encryption**: TLS or SSL
- **Sender email**: address displayed as sender

Email notifications can be used for:

- Session invitations
- Vote links
- Screening reminders

### Application Settings

Other customizable settings include:

- **Instance name**: customize the name displayed in the interface
- **Default session options**: pre-filled values when creating new sessions
- **Scheduler behavior**: check intervals for automatic tasks

> **Tip**: configure SMTP with a dedicated address (e.g., `cinema@yourdomain.com`) so invitations look professional.

config-export.title: Export and Import
config-export.summary: Back up and restore your complete configuration with conflict management.
config-export.content:
## Configuration Export and Import

Theatarr allows you to **export** and **import** your complete configuration, useful for backups or migration to a new server.

### Export Configuration

From **Settings > Export/Import**, click **Export**.

The export generates an encrypted JSON file containing:

- **Sessions**: all sessions and their workflows
- **Services**: connected service configurations (API keys are encrypted)
- **Templates**: custom display templates
- **Settings**: general application configuration
- **Users**: accounts and roles (passwords excluded)
- **Votes and quizzes**: history of created votes and quizzes

### Store the File Securely

The exported file contains sensitive information (encrypted API keys, network configurations). Keep it in a **secure location**:

- External hard drive
- Encrypted cloud service
- Password manager

### Import a Configuration

To restore a configuration:

1. Click **Import**
2. Select the exported JSON file
3. Choose the **conflict resolution strategy**

### Conflict Resolution

When data already exists in the instance, three strategies are available:

- **Skip**: keeps existing data, only imports new entries
- **Overwrite**: replaces existing data with the file's data
- **Merge**: intelligently combines data (keeps the most recent)

### Use Cases

#### Regular Backup

Export your configuration regularly (e.g., monthly) to have a backup in case of problems.

#### Server Migration

1. Export from the old server
2. Install Theatarr on the new server
3. Import the configuration
4. Update service IP addresses if necessary

#### Configuration Sharing

Share your configuration (without API keys) with a friend who wants to replicate your setup.

> **Important**: after an import, verify that all services are still accessible by running a **connection test** for each one.

config-users.title: User Management
config-users.summary: Create accounts, assign roles and manage admin and portal access.
config-users.content:
## User Management

Theatarr has a **user management** system with two access levels.

### Available Roles

#### Administrator

Administrators have access to **all features**:

- Create and manage cinema sessions
- Configure services and workflows
- Manage votes and quizzes
- Administer user accounts
- Access system logs
- Export/import configuration

#### User

Standard users only access the **portal**:

- View sessions they are invited to
- Participate in votes
- Take quizzes
- View their statistics
- Manage their profile

### Create an Account

From **Users** in the admin menu:

1. Click **New user**
2. Enter the information:
   - **Username**: login identifier
   - **Full name**: name displayed in the interface
   - **Email**: email address (for notifications)
   - **Password**: initial password
   - **Role**: Administrator or User
3. Click **Create**

### Edit an Account

From the user list, click on an account to edit:

- Name and email
- Role (promotion or demotion)
- Password (reset)

### User Profile

Each user can edit their own profile from the **user menu** in the top right:

- Change their display name
- Update their email
- Change their password

### Best Practices

- Create a dedicated **admin** account and a separate **user** account for your daily use
- Assign the **user** role to your regular guests so they can easily vote and participate
- Use **strong passwords** for administrator accounts
- For occasional guests, use **token links** for voting instead (no account needed)

> **Tip**: create accounts for your regular guests. They can accumulate statistics (movies watched, votes, quizzes) and see their history on the portal.

portal-overview.title: Portal Overview
portal-overview.summary: Discover the home page, sessions, votes and statistics of the user portal.
portal-overview.content:
## The User Portal

The portal is the interface dedicated to **participants** of your movie nights. It offers a simplified experience optimized for mobile.

### Home Page

The portal home page displays an activity summary:

- **Upcoming sessions**: next screenings you are invited to
- **Ongoing votes**: open votes awaiting your participation
- **Active quizzes**: current quizzes you can participate in
- **Quick stats**: number of movies watched, votes cast, quizzes completed

### My Sessions

The sessions page is organized in tabs:

- **Upcoming**: scheduled sessions you are invited to
- **All**: complete history of your sessions
- **To rate**: finished sessions awaiting your review/rating

For each session, you see:

- Session name and date
- The movie (if revealed) with its poster
- Your status (invited, confirmed, present)
- A badge indicating the mode (fixed, vote, mystery)

### My Votes

Find all votes you participate in:

- Open votes awaiting your choice
- Closed votes with results
- Your participation history

### My Quizzes

Access available quizzes:

- Ongoing quizzes: join and answer
- Finished quizzes: view your scores and ranking

### Statistics

The portal calculates your **personal statistics**:

- Total number of movies watched via Theatarr
- Number of votes you participated in
- Average quiz score
- Most watched movie genres
- Participation history

### Profile

Access your personal settings:

- Change your name and email
- Change your password
- Choose your preferred language and theme

> **Tip**: add the portal as a shortcut on your phone's home screen for quick access on the day of the screening.

portal-voting.title: Participate in a Vote
portal-voting.summary: Receive an invitation, vote for a movie and follow results in real time.
portal-voting.content:
## Participate in a Vote

As a participant, you can vote for the next screening's movie in two ways: via your **portal account** or via a **participation link** (token).

### Access the Vote

#### Via the Portal

If you have a Theatarr account:

1. Log in to the portal
2. Open votes appear on the home page
3. Click on a vote to access the voting page

#### Via a Token Link

If you received a participation link:

1. Open the link in your browser
2. You access the voting page directly
3. No login is required

### Vote

The voting page displays the **proposed movies** with for each:

- The movie poster
- Title and year
- TMDB rating
- Synopsis
- Genres

To vote:

1. Browse the proposed movies
2. Click on the movie(s) of your choice (depending on the number of votes allowed)
3. Confirm your vote

Your vote is **final**: once confirmed, it cannot be changed.

### Real-Time Results

If the organizer has enabled result display during voting:

- You see the movie **ranking** updated live
- The number of votes for each movie is visible
- The voting progress (number of people who have voted) is displayed

If results are hidden, you will only see confirmation of your vote.

### Link with Sessions

If the vote is linked to a cinema session, you may need to **accept the invitation** to the session before being able to vote. This lets the organizer know who will attend the evening.

### Reveal

The result can be revealed:

- **Immediately** after the vote closes
- **At a scheduled date**: the winning movie stays secret until the chosen moment
- **Live**: during the evening, on the wallmount

> **Tip**: check the synopses and ratings to make an informed choice. The proposed movies are generally in the organizer's library, so they're available for quality screening.

portal-quiz.title: Participate in a Quiz
portal-quiz.summary: Join a quiz, answer questions, view scores and the final leaderboard.
portal-quiz.content:
## Participate in a Quiz

Quizzes are a fun activity offered before, during or after cinema screenings. Test your knowledge and challenge your friends!

### Join a Quiz

From the portal:

1. An active quiz appears on the home page
2. Click **Join** to enter the quiz
3. Wait for the organizer to launch the questions

### Quiz Flow

The quiz runs in **real time**:

1. A question is displayed on your screen
2. Answer choices are presented (2 to 6 options)
3. A **countdown** shows the time remaining to answer
4. Select your answer before time runs out
5. If a **hint** is available, it may appear after a certain delay

### Scoring System

The score is calculated based on:

- **Correct answer**: points awarded
- **Speed**: the faster you answer, the more points you earn
- **No answer**: 0 points if time runs out
- **Wrong answer**: 0 points (no penalty)

### Feedback Between Questions

If the organizer has enabled feedback:

- The **correct answer** is shown after each question
- **Statistics** show the percentage of players who chose each answer
- The **intermediate leaderboard** is updated

### Live Leaderboard

If live results are enabled, you can see:

- Your position in the ranking
- Other participants' scores
- The ranking evolution question by question

### Final Leaderboard

At the end of the quiz, the **final leaderboard** is displayed with:

- The podium (1st, 2nd, 3rd)
- Each participant's score
- Number of correct answers
- Average response time

The leaderboard can also be displayed on the **wallmount** for the entire room to see the results.

### Tips for Playing Well

- Read the question **completely** before answering
- Speed matters: don't overthink if you're hesitating
- Use the **hint** if available, it doesn't cost any points
- Stay focused: time flies!

> **Tip**: auto-generated "Film & TV" quizzes are in English. If you're unsure about a term, rely on context and proper nouns.
